page: Microsoft Azure M16bs_v3 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the MBSMediumMemoryv3 family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel Xeon 8473C cores running at 4.0 GHz, with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on external block storage with Premium Storage capabilities.

In benchmark testing, the M16bs_v3 demonstrates strong single-core capabilities. Its Geekbench single-core score of 2213.0 and text processing score of 2801.0 both rank in the top tier (top 10%). Single-threaded gzip compression is also strong at 32.93 GB/sec. Multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks generally fall within the average range, with uncached large-block read bandwidth at 108.38 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 67.71 GB/sec. For lightweight machine learning tasks, the server achieves a top-tier text generation speed of 333.36 tokens per second using a small 135M parameter LLM, though performance scales down to an average 16.02 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the M16bs_v3 offers a high-density memory profile relative to its core count, making it a viable option for workloads requiring substantial memory without the overhead of excess vCPUs. However, the lack of local storage requires users to provision external block storage, which may introduce latency and additional configuration considerations. The server is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, text processing, software compilation, and light LLM inference tasks.
